svg.title: Flower Anatomy Drag & Drop
svg.desc: A self-contained flower anatomy learning interface. Ten word-bank links preview labels one at a time. Hint, Check Answer, and Reset open internal SVG popup groups. The answer key can reveal every label. No scripts, images, or external assets are used.

g.text: Look closely. Connect each structure with the job it does.
Meet the parts of a flower
LEARNING MODE / SELECT A TILE TO PREVIEW ITS MATCH
Select a word-bank tile to preview
its correct place on the flower.
Look at the structure each empty
slot points to. Compare its shape.
Open the answer key, or reset
to return to the empty diagram.
Pollen moves from anther to stigma.
A pollen tube can grow toward an ovule.
Tap or click a tile. Preview one match at a time.
Observe the details. Discover the whole.

g.title: petal — A colorful leaf-like part that attracts pollinators.
g.text: PETAL / A colorful leaf-like part that attracts pollinators.

g.title: anther — The pollen-producing tip of a stamen.
g.text: ANTHER / The pollen-producing tip of a stamen.

g.title: filament — The slender stalk that supports an anther.
g.text: FILAMENT / The slender stalk that supports an anther.

g.title: stamen — The male structure: anther and filament.
g.text: STAMEN / The male structure: anther and filament.

g.title: sepal — A green outer part that protects the flower bud.
g.text: SEPAL / A green outer part that protects the flower bud.

g.title: stigma — The sticky surface that receives pollen.
g.text: STIGMA / The sticky surface that receives pollen.

g.title: style — The stalk connecting the stigma and ovary.
g.text: STYLE / The stalk connecting the stigma and ovary.

g.title: ovary — The part of the pistil that contains ovules.
g.text: OVARY / The part of the pistil that contains ovules.

g.title: receptacle — The stem tip where the flower parts attach.
g.text: RECEPTACLE / The stem tip where the flower parts attach.

g.title: pistil — The female structure: stigma, style, and ovary.
g.text: PISTIL / The female structure: stigma, style, and ovary.
ANSWER KEY / All 10 labels revealed. Use Reset to practice again.

g.aria-label: Start with what you can see.
g.text: Start with what you can see.
A flower has protective parts and reproductive parts.
Petals attract pollinators; sepals protect the bud.
The anther makes pollen; the filament supports it.
Pollen arrives at the stigma. Ovules are inside the ovary.
After fertilization, an ovule can become a seed.
Compare each numbered target with its structure.
Whole structures include smaller parts: stamen ≠ anther; pistil ≠ ovary.
Return to the flower with all ten label slots empty.
Choose a different word, follow its arrow,
and notice how the parts work together.
